problem: A car is traveling along a straight road to a particular destination. The remaining distance $D(t)$ varies according to the differential equation ${D}^{′}(t)=-rD(t),$ where $t$ is the time, measured in hours, and $r>0.$ Two hours into the journey, the remaining distance is three-quarters of the journey's total distance. How long does it take for the remaining distance to reduce to one-third of the journey's total distance? Round your answer to one decimal place.

examples.knowledge_point: Computing an Unknown Time Given an Exponential Growth or Decay Model With an Unknown Rate
examples.problem: During an experiment, the weight $W(t)$ of an object varies according to the differential equation $W'(t) = -r W(t),$ where $t$ is the time, measured in hours, and $r > 0.$ It is known that the object's weight reduces by three-quarters after the first two hours. How long does it take for the object's weight to reduce to one-sixth of its original weight? Round your answer to one decimal place.
examples.worked_solution:
The general solution to the given differential equation is

$$
W(t) = W_0 e^{-rt},
$$

where $W_0$ is the weight when $t=0.$

Let $t_1$ be the time when the weight equals $\dfrac{1}{6}W_0.$ Then, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}W({t}_{1}) & =\frac{1}{6}{W}_{0}\,⇒\,{W}_{0}{e}^{-r{t}_{1}}=\frac{1}{6}{W}_{0}.\end{aligned}
$$

We solve this equation for $t_1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{W}_{0}{e}^{-r{t}_{1}} & =\frac{1}{6}{W}_{0} \\ \cancel{{W}_{0}}{e}^{-r{t}_{1}} & =\frac{1}{6}\cancel{{W}_{0}} \\ {e}^{-r{t}_{1}} & =\frac{1}{6} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-r{t}_{1}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{6}) \\ -r{t}_{1} & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡6 \\ {t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡6}{r}\,\,(∗)\end{aligned}
$$

We now need to calculate $r.$ We're told that the weight reduces by three-quarters after the first two hours. Therefore, one-quarter of the weight remains, and we have

$$
W(2) = \dfrac{1}{4}W_0\quad \Rightarrow\quad W_0e^{-2r} = \dfrac{1}{4}W_0
$$

We solve this equation for $r,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{W}_{0}{e}^{-2r} & =\frac{1}{4}{W}_{0} \\ \cancel{{W}_{0}}{e}^{-2r} & =\frac{1}{4}\cancel{{W}_{0}} \\ {e}^{-2r} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-2r}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{4}) \\ -2r & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ r & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ r & =\operatorname{ln}⁡{4}^{1/2} \\ r & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this into $(*)$ and evaluating, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡6}{r} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & ≈2.6\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place. 

Therefore, we conclude that it takes approximately $2.6$ hours for the weight to reduce to one-sixth of its original weight.

feedback.problem:
The rate at which the number of active users of a mobile app decreases $U(t),$ after $t$ weeks from launch, can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}U}{\text{d}t}=-0.04U.
$$

If there are $40\,000$ active users at launch, how many weeks does it take for the number of active users to decrease to $20\,000?$  Round your answer to the nearest week.
feedback.worked_solution:
We model the number of active users using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}U}{\text{d}t}=-0.04U.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
U(t)={U}_{0}\,{e}^{-0.04t},
$$

where ${U}_{0}$ is the initial number of active users.

We're told that there are $40\,000$ active users at launch, so we have ${U}_{0}=40\,000.$

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the number of active users has decreased to $20\,000.$ That is,

$$
U({t}_{1})=20\,000.
$$

We solve the above equation for ${t}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}20\,000 & =40\,000{e}^{-0.04{t}_{1}} \\ \frac{20\,000}{40\,000} & ={e}^{-0.04{t}_{1}} \\ 0.5 & ={e}^{-0.04{t}_{1}} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.5) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-0.04{t}_{1}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.5) & =-0.04{t}_{1} \\ {t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.5)}{-0.04} \\ {t}_{1} & ≈17.329\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we conclude that it takes $17$ weeks for the number of active users to decrease to $20\,000.$
